notes.about: SWOT RiverSP reach_q at this reach (knowledge: datasets/swot-river-lake.md)
notes.text: Seen while exploring calendar 2024 at reach 74210000331 against USGS-07374000, Version D, 50 pairs within 15 minutes. The three passes with reach_q 2 all fall at low stage (gauge 1.47 to 3.51 m of a 1.47 to 10.33 m range); their departures from the median level difference have a spread of 0.798 m against 0.162 m for the 47 passes with reach_q 1, and one (2024-10-30, the lowest stage of the year) is 1.776 m low. The product's stated uncertainty for that pass is 0.095 m, the median, so wse_u does not warn of it. The dataset concept says reach_q is a categorical gate and does not say what happens to a comparison when it is not applied. Unflagged passes at low stage are fine (lowest third of stage, 15 pairs, spread 0.078 m), so it is the flag and not low water that marks them.

notes.about: SWOT RiverSP dark_frac and wse_u on an unflagged pass (knowledge: datasets/swot-river-lake.md)
notes.text: Seen while exploring the same record. One pass with reach_q 1 (2024-03-26, gauge 7.68 m) is 0.939 m above the rest. It has the highest dark_frac of the year (0.692; the next highest third starts at 0.026) and the largest stated uncertainty (wse_u 0.296 m against a median of 0.096 m). So here the quality flag missed a bad pass that dark_frac and wse_u both mark. One pass in one year: enough to warn, not enough to set a threshold. With it and the three flagged passes left out the residual spread about the gain line is 0.082 m, below the product's median stated uncertainty.

notes.about: knowledge: recipes/swot-gauge-confrontation.md, the worked example for Baton Rouge 2024
notes.text: Seen while exploring. The recipe's worked example scores all 50 pairs: change correlation +0.9567 and change RMSD 0.3823 m, which it reads as about four times the product's stated precision. Recomputed here identically (LOOK-013). With the three passes flagged reach_q 2 left out, the same scores are +0.9896 and 0.1859 m on 46 changes (LOOK-014). So most of the disagreement the worked example reports is three flagged passes, and the recipe has no step that says to apply the product's quality gate before scoring.

notes.about: pairing tolerance below the gauge's reporting interval
notes.text: Seen while exploring. Pairing within 5 minutes keeps 31 of 52 passes, because the gauge reports every 15 minutes; 15 minutes keeps 50 and 60 minutes keeps all 52 with the same spread (0.298 m and 0.293 m) and, with the flag screen, a gain of 1.0121 and 1.0115. A tolerance tighter than the gauge interval only throws passes away.
